note.text:
History is the study of the past: what people did, how they lived and why things changed. Historians work from evidence called sources.
Kinds of sources:
• oral sources: stories, songs, proverbs and memories passed on by word of mouth, for example by elders and griots;
• written sources: books, letters, newspapers, records and inscriptions;
• material (archaeological) sources: objects and remains from the past, such as tools, pottery, bones, coins and buildings.
The time before writing is called prehistory; we learn about it mainly from material sources found by archaeologists.
Why study history? To understand how our communities and country came to be, to learn from the past, to respect other peoples, and to keep our heritage alive.

worked_example.problem: To learn how her village began, Asong listens to her grandfather’s story, reads an old letter at the mission, and looks at an old iron hoe kept by the chief. Which kind of source is each one?
steps: The grandfather’s story is passed on by word of mouth: an oral source.
The letter is written: a written source.
The iron hoe is an object from the past: a material source.
worked_example.answer: Story: oral. Letter: written. Hoe: material.

cards.idea: Sources can be oral (spoken), written, or material (objects and remains).
example: A griot’s song is oral; a diary is written; a clay pot is material.

cards.idea: Studying history helps us understand our community, learn from the past and keep our heritage.
example: Knowing how a festival began helps us understand why it matters.
